reply_text:
Hunting for the source of "112", then I'll check whether the loops' queue can actually move it overnight.㊥ (progress by morning) Both loops are running and working on rows. I've set up an overnight watch so that a loop which stops or runs out of work wakes me to restart or refill it, instead of sitting idle until you're back. Expect a few closures by morning, not dozens. Each loop works one row at a time, and only about 14 open problems have rows in the ledgers right now.

㊩ ("it says there are 112 open problems") I don't get 112. `~/topo-watch/check.py` counts by real `sorry`/`admit` in `problems/t*/lean`, and it reports 93 open, 10 with no Lean file yet, and 153 placeholders. Where are you seeing 112? I'll report against whichever counter you mean.

🈖 (why the progress will be modest)
- **Coverage.** The two ledgers have live rows for only about 14 problems (t98J02, t99J04, t99J05, t94J09, t96A07, t95A04, t02A02, t00J07, t94A08, …). The others get rows only when a strategy checkpoint elects new routes.
- **topo1 will need a refill.** After its 3 remaining rows, topo1 reaches its refill checkpoint. The previous one answered "terminal": every other route was held by the stop-after-two rule. If that happens again, the loop pauses, which happened on 09-29 too and needed a manual refill.
- **topo2 is refilling itself.** Its strategy step wrote four new rows today (`routes-2026-10-10-*`).
- **Quota is fine.** The Codex weekly window is at 12%.

㊢ (what I set up) `~/topo-watch/overnight-watch.sh` is running under bg.py (`bg-1791603763559-308`). Every 10 minutes it checks both units. If either is inactive, or its log has been silent for 75 minutes, it bells me in work mode to act as owner: refill a paused ledger, or repair and relaunch a stopped loop. It sends at most one bell per loop every 90 minutes. I set its end time to "tomorrow 09:00" UTC, which works out to 10-11 09:00, a day later than I meant. It's harmless and covers your whole day; `bg.py kill` stops it.

㊢ (first results since restart) Two reviews have come back. The t98J02 counterexamples adapter passed review, but t98J02 still has one `sorry`, so it doesn't count as closed yet. The t96A07 closure attempt stopped and is under review now. To compare in the morning, run `~/topo-watch/check.py`; it prints closures and reopenings since the last check.
